description: Esan team in NASA Space Apps
summary: NASAftESAN built a workflow that harmonizes active-fire (hot spot) detections from two NASA sensors — MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) — into a single, comparable view for Peruvian farmland. Using NASA FIRMS data services (WFS feeds for South America: fires_modis_7days and fires_snpp_7days, plus the 7-day CSV as an offline backup) loaded in QGIS, the team aligns both sensors over the same farming areas and time window so that differences in resolution, brightness, fire radiative power (FRP) and confidence can be compared instead of treated as contradictory data. Farmers and local authorities lose crops and income when fires near agricultural land are detected late or inconsistently: MODIS and VIIRS often report different hot spots for the same event. A harmonized view gives earlier, more trustworthy alerts of fire risk near farms, helping producers protect fields, plan harvests and respond before a fire spreads — directly supporting farms adapting to a hotter, drier climate (Field Shift).
details:
Impact
Farmers and local authorities lose crops and income when fires near agricultural land are detected late or inconsistently: MODIS and VIIRS often report different hot spots for the same event. A harmonized view gives earlier, more trustworthy alerts of fire risk near farms, helping producers protect fields, plan harvests and respond before a fire spreads — directly supporting farms adapting to a hotter, drier climate (Field Shift).

How it works (Validity)
The harmonization compares both sensors over the same region and 7-day window: spatial resolution (MODIS 1 km vs VIIRS 375 m), detection attributes (brightness, FRP, confidence) and coverage are documented side by side, and the FIRMS 7-day CSV export serves as a reproducible backup dataset so any judge can reload the same data in QGIS and verify the comparison.

Creativity
The project fuses an official 2026 challenge (Field Shift) with a challenge this same team proposed last year ('Perú is password') that became the official 'Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots' challenge — turning last year's idea into this year's working data pipeline for agriculture.

Relevance
This solution addresses the Field Shift challenge directly: it uses NASA Earth observation data to help farms adapt to changing fire risk, giving Peruvian producers a practical, comparable view of active fires near their fields.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI)
AI tools were used only to improve the system's UX/UI design and to generate the project video. All data processing, analysis and development were done by the team.
